$schema_doc: Golden-Route fixtures (E03-T5, erweitert in E10-T3; docs/07-testing-qa.md §3b). Types: 'distance' (route length within ±tolerance), 'restriction' (🔴 safety: small profile MUST enter forbidden_bbox, large/heavy profile MUST NOT — both directions asserted; kind is maxheight|maxweight|maxwidth), 'monotonic' (route duration non-decreasing over an ascending profile list — catches swapped profile→costing mappings), 'no_route' (expects NO_ROUTE), 'eta' (ETA-Plausibilität: simulator drives the route's own geometry at the planned pace with speed_factor 1.0; |actual arrival − first published ETA| must stay < max_eta_error of the planned duration). Region selection: the runner (e2e/golden-routes/runner.test.ts) runs only cases whose 'region' equals GOLDEN_REGION (li|de, default li). LI cases run in the per-PR CI job 'golden-routes-li' (Merge-Blocker, retry:0, bail:1 — a failed safety/monotonic case HARD-ABORTS with no retry/tolerance). DE cases run only in the nightly 'golden-routes-de' job. 'nightly_only':true excludes a case unless GOLDEN_NIGHTLY=1 — used for the 'eta' case, which burns one second of WALL CLOCK per simulated second and must not sit in a per-PR gate; the nightly jobs set the flag. 'unverified':true marks a case whose expected value or restriction has NOT been confirmed against a live Valhalla run in this sandbox (Overpass/OSM-API/geofabrik are egress-blocked here); the nightly DE job runs continue-on-error so unverified failures are logged, not blocking. HOW A RESTRICTION CASE BECOMES VERIFIED (E10-T3): do NOT look the way up on overpass — run scripts/osm-restriction-provenance.sh against THE SAME PBF the nightly graph is built from. It extracts every maxheight/maxweight/maxwidth way inside each case's forbidden_bbox and emits a ready-to-paste 'restriction' block with the real osm_way_id + tag value. That is stronger evidence than Overpass: it proves the tag exists in the ROUTED dataset, not merely in today's live OSM. Its 'discover' mode lists the strongest real candidates in a region so a case built on an unconfirmed location can be REPLACED by a tagged one instead of being guessed into shape. Only after that run: fill osm_way_id/value/source, freeze expected_distance_m from the observed run, and flip unverified:false. NEVER hand-fill an osm_way_id or a maxheight value — a fabricated provenance entry makes an unverified case LOOK verified, which is worse than an admitted gap. SAFETY-DEMO (acceptance #3): LI has no map-restriction data, so the restriction assertion cannot be exercised on LI — see the note on the DE restriction cases for exactly how a swapped height/weight mapping makes them fail; on LI the monotonic case is the closest available guard (a swapped top_speed/avg_speed mapping that made a larger vehicle route faster would break its non-decreasing assertion), and scripts/runbook-smoke.sh proves the same property end-to-end against a stub router with NO map data at all.

cases.provenance: E10-T3: the DE counterpart of li-monotonic-vaduz-schaan. Nuremberg -> Fuerth is a short, densely-connected urban pair, so all three profiles are expected to be routable. Profiles ascend in size/weight and DESCEND in avg_speed_kmh (Kastenwagen 110 -> Camper 95 -> Alkoven 7.5t 80), so duration must be non-decreasing even on identical geometry. Why a DE monotonic case at all when LI already has one: the profile->costing mapping is exercised against a REAL road network with motorway/urban mix and actual truck restrictions here, whereas the LI graph is a single valley road — a mapping bug that only manifests where truck costing has choices to make would be invisible on LI. Coordinates are the two city centres (public map estimate); NOT yet routed against the DE graph.

cases.todo: E10-T3 — confirm OFFLINE, from the same germany PBF the nightly graph is built from: `scripts/osm-restriction-provenance.sh verify <pbf>` prints every maxheight way inside this case's forbidden_bbox with its way-id and tag value, and emits the ready-to-paste 'restriction' block. (Overpass/OSM-API are egress-blocked in the build sandbox, and the PBF is the better source anyway: it proves the tag is in the ROUTED dataset.) Then adjust origin/destination + forbidden_bbox so the low profile's natural path runs under the bridge. SAFETY-DEMO: with the correct data, swapping height<->weight in apps/core/src/routing/profileMapping.ts makes the tall profile's height be read as its (small) weight, so Valhalla stops avoiding the low bridge -> the large-profile route enters forbidden_bbox -> this case FAILS (hard). That is the concrete proof the safety gate catches a broken mapping.

cases.todo: E10-T3 — the FIRST and currently only Breitenfall (Breite×1). NOTHING in this case is confirmed: coordinates are an approximate placement of the Roedertor gate passage, the 2.2 m value is a plausible signed width for a medieval gate but has NOT been read from any dataset, and the OSM way-id is unknown. Run `scripts/osm-restriction-provenance.sh verify <germany.pbf>` for the real way-id + maxwidth. TWO ways this case can turn out unusable, and both are fine outcomes of the verify run: (a) no maxwidth is tagged on the gate passage, or (b) the passage is not routable for motor vehicles at all, in which case the small profile cannot traverse the bbox and the runner fails the case as VACUOUS by design (that assertion exists precisely so a restriction case cannot pass for the wrong reason). In either case replace it from `discover maxwidth`, which lists the real narrow ways in the extract sorted by how binding they are. Do NOT hand-edit a way-id in.

Chosen as a DIFFERENT physical category from the height (railway bridges) and weight (motorway river bridges) cases, so the width dimension is not just a re-skin of an existing case.
